utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, on Monday morning you asked me to address two queries, so just briefly to respond to the Chamber. With respect to VG-17 and its omission from the 12th of September document or schedule, that was an oversight. I have provided a new updated version of that to the -- to the court officer as well as to the Defence counsel this morning, which includes all of the intended witnesses until the end of the Prosecution case. And the second query had to do with VG-002. The Prosecution will be filing a motion with respect to the submission of written testimony in lieu of oral evidence this morning, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You may sit. And you may begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Could the court usher please hand to the witness the pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-89, you've been granted certain protective measures by the Trial Chamber. I would like to direct your attention to the sheet before you. That's a pseudonym sheet. Do you recognise your name on that sheet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does your date of birth also appear on that sheet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-89, could you please sign that sheet at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, the Prosecution tenders the pseudonym sheet into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be admitted as Exhibit P103 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-89, how old were you in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you in school in the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What school did you attend?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Vuk Karadzic Primary School in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What year in school were you at the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Year 8, class D.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What municipality or town did you live in during May 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: In Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you live in a particular settlement within Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. Nova Mahala, it was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who did you live with in the Nova Mahala settlement of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: With my grandmother and my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How long did you live in Visegrad prior to 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Eight years.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At the beginning of May 1992, who occupied the town of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you aware of a particular division of the Serb soldiers that were occupying Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The Uzice Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How long were the Uzice Corps in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Until the 19th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after the Uzice Corps left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Serb paramilitary units started taking away and killing Muslim people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is there a particular incident that you heard of immediately after the Uzice Corps left Visegrad involving the Serb paramilitary units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Behija Zukic was killed, and she used to own a grocery store in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where was this grocery store in relation to the Nova Mahala settlement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Across the street from the cinema.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the date that you heard of the killing of Behija Zukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where were you when you heard of her death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: In the 22nd December Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who informed you of her death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Local Muslim residents.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to Behija Zukic, did she own any type of car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: A Volkswagen Passat, burgundy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was this Passat notable within the Visegrad municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. At that time it was the best car in town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were there any other red Volkswagen Passats in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to return to the 21st of May, 1992. After you heard of -- well, what -- what is it that you were told by the local Muslim residents of Behija Zukic's death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I was told that Behija Zukic was killed, whereas her husband and son had been taken away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was any name mentioned in conjunction with her death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to go anywhere on the 21st of May, 1992, after you learned of Behija Zukic's death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It might be as well just to find out exactly what he heard about Milan Lukic in relation to Behija Zukic's death.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-89, what exactly did you hear about Milan Lukic in relation to the death of Behija Zukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I heard that Milan Lukic killed Behija Zukic, took away her husband and son, and seized her car.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did you go after learning of Behija Zukic's death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Towards the Muslim cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where's the Muslim cemetery located in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: At the exit from the town towards Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you go towards the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: In the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was anyone with you when you went to the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: A friend was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you comfortable providing your friend's name, or would you like to go into closed session for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: It is all right for me to say his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please use the first name of your friend.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Almir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How old was Almir at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you see when you and Almir arrived at the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We saw around a hundred people at the Muslim cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you observed these a hundred people, where were you and Almir at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Across the street from the cemetery, next to the Ina petrol station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how far were you from the group of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: A hundred and fifty metres or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you elevated or on ground level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: As these people were coming, we were on slightly higher ground, and then as they went on moving they went higher than -- than we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Whose funeral were you watching?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Behija Zukic's funeral and another Muslim nicknamed Medo and his wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did anything happen towards the end of the funeral?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. A car showed up -- or, rather, a small truck. We call it a small TAM truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were there any other vehicles with this TAM truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, a smaller vehicle, but I can't remember which type. At any rate, it was not the burgundy Volkswagen Passat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe the TAM truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: A small TAM truck, dark green with tarpaulin in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did the TAM truck and this other car go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: They parked outside the entrance to the Muslim cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where was this entrance in relation to where you and Almir were at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Approximately 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you still see the group that was present at the funeral along with the truck and the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After the truck and the car pulled up, what occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: People started coming back from the cemetery, and then the men from the truck and that little car stopped them at the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How many men got out of the truck and car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Four or five.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What were these four or five men wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Camouflage army uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who did you believe them to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Serb paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you later learn [Realtime transcript read in error, "then"] the names or name of any of the individuals who exited either the truck or the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe in line 9 of the transcript it says, "did you later then." The question that was posed was, "did you later learn the names." If there could be a correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who did you see that exited the truck that you later learned the name of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe what happened as the people exited from the funeral of Behija Zukic and towards Milan Lukic and the other Serb soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan Lukic and the others approached them, told them something, but we couldn't hear what because we were too far away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After Milan Lukic and the others approached the group and told them something, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: They started shoving the Muslims in the back of the TAM truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you recognise the Muslims that were being shoved in the back of the TAM truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: No. I knew some of them by sight, but they were older people that I didn't know at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how many Muslims were shoved into the back of the TAM truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Around 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did the other people besides these 15 Muslims do when this was occurring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: They started running in a panic all across the cemetery towards the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, was Milan Lukic and the other soldiers armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you see after these Muslims were placed into the TAM truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: They went down the main street into town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say "they," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I mean those two cars and the Serb soldiers who took away the Muslim civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just for clarification, are you referring to two cars or the car and the TAM truck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I mean one car and one little TAM truck. At that moment, I noticed that the other vehicle was white.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you ever see those 15 Muslims again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I had not seen much of them before, but after that I hadn't heard or seen them anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After the funeral of Behija Zukic, did there come a time where you and your mother sought to leave the Visegrad area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately when was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: In the first week of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the reason that you and your mother attempted to leave Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: So as not to meet the same fate as those people who had been taken away along with many others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How were you and your mother planning to leave Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We planned to leave in a convoy to Macedonia, to Skopje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where was this convoy leaving from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: From a location between the Borac department store in town and a sports hall nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you and your mother go to meet this convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Early in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you and your mother arrived in the area of the Borac department store and the sports hall, did you see anyone else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, around a hundred and fifty Muslims who were also trying to leave with the same convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anyone that was amongst these 150 Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was this another family from your settlement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. More than one family.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you and your mother go over and join this family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the name of this family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Dervisevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after you and your mother met with this family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes later, the burgundy Volkswagen Passat appeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When the Volkswagen Passat appeared, did you see anyone inside of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how far was the Volkswagen Passat from you when it first arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: 20 metres or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone got out of the Volkswagen Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How many people did you see exit the Volkswagen Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we did not get the complete answer. VG-89, how many people did you see exit the Volkswagen Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Two.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Had you seen these two men before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When was the one time that you had seen these two men before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: At Behija Zukic's funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you physically describe each of these two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. One of them was 25, 26 years old, tall, around 195 [Realtime transcript read in error, "125"] centimetres, black hair, wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How would you describe the other man?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that we have mistake in translation. Page 11, line 4. It is not 125 centimetres. Witness said different, different measure in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I heard 195.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's also what I heard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other one was short and stocky, not more than 170 centimetres tall, older, perhaps 35 years old, and he had a moustache, black hair and black moustache, also wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were these men carrying anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What were they carrying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The shorter one had an automatic rifle, and the taller one had a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After these two men arrived where did they go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: They approached this crowd of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened as these two men approached the crowd of a hundred and fifty Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: First, they were looking for a man by name, but when they realised he wasn't there, then the taller one who had some sort of list in his hands, when the buses arrived he told the people which bus to board.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Prior to the buses arriving, did you see any type of conversation between this taller man and anyone that was in the group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you observe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He approached my friend's sister, addressed her by name and said she was -- she used to be his schoolmate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did your friend's sister say anything back at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. She greeted him and addressed him by name as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What name did your friend's sister use when she greeted this taller man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How far were you from Milan Lukic when your friend's sister greeted him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I was next to him, standing to his left in this little circle of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say next to him, how far was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Half a metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What view of his face did you have during this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you able to view Milan Lukic from the front or side during this conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: From the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how long did Milan Lukic engage in conversation with your friend's sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After this conversation, what occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The buses arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did the group of a hundred and fifty people do after the buses arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: They started getting onto the buses just as the tall man I didn't know at the time was telling them to as to who should go where.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How many buses were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How were the a hundred and fifty Muslims being told to get onto the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The women and children went to some of the buses, and the men were taken separately to some other buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The person that your friend's sister identified as Milan Lukic, what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He was standing at the bus door, and he was telling everyone where to go. He was holding slips of paper in his hand with names of people on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you and your mother get onto one of the buses?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What bus did you get onto?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The second one, the second one in line.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did you and your mother sit after -- well, when you first got onto the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I went to the back of the bus with my friend, and my mother was about five or six rows in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who is this friend that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Almir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At some point in time, did you relocate by your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: My friend's sister took us there because we were making too much noise in the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did you sit by your mother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Right next to her. My mother had the window seat, and then as soon as I came she moved over, and I took the window seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did the buses then depart Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At some point in time after the buses left Visegrad, were they stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where were they stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: At the border to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was there a particular village or town in which the buses were stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Jagodina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe what happened when the buses were stopped in Jagodina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We were still sitting in that bus for about 20 minutes. We didn't know what was going on, and we didn't have their permission to leave the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you're saying "their permission," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The permission of the Serbs who were there. There was a car tailing us, tailing the last bus in our convoy. The drivers were the only Serbs there, and they were allowed to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This car that was tailing you, could you please tell us what car that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The same car that was parked there before we started out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the make of that car, and who did it formally belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: It was a Volkswagen Passat, the one that used to belong to the Zukic family, but during the war it was driven by Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you see any individuals that you saw prior in the square when the buses were stopped in Jagodina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, just a single person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did you again see Milan Lukic when the buses stopped in Jagodina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: When we were on our way back to Visegrad. The men were on the last bus. They left them there, but they took us back. As the bus was moving back in the same direction and turning, I saw Milan Lukic line up all the men in a single line next to the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just to backtrack a little bit, at some point in time were the buses turned away from proceeding towards Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. They were on their way back to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How were you informed of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The Serb driver came back onto the bus, and he said, "We've got to take you back to Visegrad."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did the people on the bus react when they were told this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Most started crying.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is that the point in time in which the buses turned around to head back towards Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, and everybody on those buses were looking out to see what would happen to that last bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was it at the point in time that the buses were turning around that you were able to see Milan Lukic in the single line of men next to the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: That's right. The road was narrow at that point, and it took some time for the buses to turn around. I had about five or six minutes to notice Milan Lukic. He was facing in my direction, and the men who were lined up faced away from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was Milan Lukic carrying anything at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The same sniper rifle that I had seen him carry at the parking lot before we started out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened as your bus proceeded past the line of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: They sent us back to that house in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say "they," are you referring to you and your mother, along with the rest of the Muslims that were with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. The three buses were sent back, and the one bus was held back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Which one bus was held back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The fourth bus with the men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After you returned to Visegrad with your mother, did you have occasion to see Milan Lukic again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have occasion to be with Almir by the bank of the river Rzav on any date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The 12th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where's the Rzav River located in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: It's near the Drina stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you and Almir go to the bank of the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: That afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you see when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Another couple of men watching another man fishing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you know the names of these men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What were their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The one fishing was called Tuka Bogdanovic. He was a neighbour of mine. And the man watching, his name was Kasim Fehric.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after you and Almir arrived by the bank of the river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Two more men turned up who were armed, and they walked up to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you immediately recognise these two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who were these two men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Budimir Kovacevic, who was the husband of my schoolmaster in elementary school, Marija Kovacevic. The other one was Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was Milan Lukic wearing on the 12th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He was wearing military uniform, that same sniper rifle, but this was the first time I saw him wear a cap with a cockade on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When Milan Lukic and this other man arrived, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: This man named Budimir told Milan, "This is the guy, Kasim Fehric."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How far were you and Almir from Milan Lukic when this initial conversation occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Two to three metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did Milan Lukic do after he was told of Kasim Fehric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He asked him, "Are you Kasim Fehric?"

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did Milan Lukic and this other man approach Kasim Fehric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Violently.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What do you mean by that description?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Well, they made threats to him immediately and said that he would have to come with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How far were you from Kasim Fehric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The same as before, about two or three metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did Kasim Fehric respond to Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He said his name was Kasim Fehric, and then he went on to say that he was on his way to hospital to get some shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic say anything back to Kasim Fehric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. He said he needn't worry, that he'd be providing all the shots he needed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How old was Kasim Fehric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After Milan Lukic made that comment to Kasim Fehric, what occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He and this man named Budimir took him along down the Lipa Street towards Dvadesetdrugog Decembra Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you and Almir do as Milan Lukic and Budimir took away Kasim Fehric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We followed them up to the midpoint of Dvadesetdrugog Decembra Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how far behind were you and Almir from Milan Lukic, Budimir, and Kasim Fehric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: No more than ten metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you able to see Milan Lukic and Kasim Fehric after they reached the 22nd of December Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, from the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How far were you from them at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: About seven or eight metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you see happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan Lukic took Kasim's cap off and gave him his own to wear, telling him that this one looked much nicer on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What kind of hat was Kasim Fehric wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Something like a beret.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was Kasim Fehric dressed in civilian or military attire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What kind of hat did Milan Lukic put on Kasim Fehric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: It was red with a cockade, some sort of a red beret.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After Milan Lukic put this hat on Kasim Fehric, what did you see happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He took him down the entire street. We only followed them halfway, and they walked all the way down to the bottom of the street, but we didn't follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Kasim Fehric again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately how much time was it between when Milan Lukic first walked up to where you and Almir were at until when you lost sight of him with Kasim Fehric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Perhaps about ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During that entire ten minutes, were you able to see Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When was the next day that you saw Milan Lukic in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The 14th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the early afternoon of the 14th of June, 1992, who were you with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Three of my friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the first names only of those friends are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Almir, Samir, Ajvaz, and me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is this the -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Could we have the last name of those men in the private session? Maybe it would be useful for some other issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Later in the afternoon on the 14th of June, 1992, were you, Almir, Samir, and Ajvaz headed to a particular place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. We were off to the Lipa neighbourhood to -- towards Almir and Samir's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Whose house was this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Taib's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did the four of you go to Taib's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We were on our way there to watch some videos since Taib had left town already.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately what time did the four of you arrive in the area of Taib's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: It was half past 3.00 in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What occurred as you approached Taib's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Almir was the only one who managed to get into the house because he was the only one who had a set of keys to the house. The three of us were stopped by a car in the middle of the street, and we didn't have time to go into the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was Almir walking in front of or behind you, Samir, and Ajvaz?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: In front.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How far in front of you was Almir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Five to six metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did Almir get into Taib's house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I unlocked the door. He had a key, and later he told me that. He couldn't even lock the door on the way out because the car suddenly turned up. Fortunately, the men in the car did not see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything as you were walking across the street towards Taib's house when Almir went into the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I just heard a voice. I didn't actually hear the car stop. I just heard a voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you recognise that voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Whose voice was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The same man who was there when we were supposed to go to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is the name of that man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After you heard Milan Lukic's voice, did you turn and face the car?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's very leading. Just ask him what he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I'd be happy to rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you do when you heard Milan Lukic's voice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I turned back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you turned back, where was the car in relation to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Some seven or eight metres away from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you facing the car, or was it behind you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Behind us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just -- at some point in time, did you turn and face the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I heard the voice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe the car that you saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: It was dark red. It was a Volkswagen Passat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How many men were inside of the Volkswagen Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Four.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who was in the passenger's -- or who was in the front passenger's seat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The same two men who were there when we were supposed to go to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who is behind the driver's seat of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Two young men in camouflage. I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd just like to be clear here. Where were these two young men in camouflage sitting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: In the back seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was there anyone sitting in the driver's seat of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who was sitting in the driver's seat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan Lukic. He was the one who called to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who was sitting in the front passenger's seat? Could you describe him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. That was the same man who had come with Milan when we were supposed to go to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you, Samir, and Ajvaz do after Milan Lukic called out from the red Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We turned around and started walking towards the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What side of the car did you walk to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The driver's side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened when you reached the driver's side of the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan Lukic asked us if we knew the man who ran a video rental nearby in the settlement called Lipa and whether we knew where he was at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after Milan Lukic asked you that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We told him we didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did he respond?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He asked for our names.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you then provide him your names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He told us to get in the back of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you then get in the back of the car with Samir and Ajvaz?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe how the three of you got in the car.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We got in the back on the driver's side. The first to get in was Samir, then -- the two young Serb soldiers were sitting next to the window. Samir got in next to them, then I got -- sat in the middle, and then Ajvaz.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: One of the Serb soldiers was in the car next to the window. Then Samir got in first. I got in after him, then Ajvaz, and the other young Serb soldier was still standing outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you got into the car and were sitting in the middle. How far were you from Milan Lukic in the driver's seat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: 10, 15 centimetres from one head to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you see if Milan Lukic had anything with him in the driver's seat of the car at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Next to him on his right, he had a sniper rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you see the end of the sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, as I was sitting in the very middle of the back seat. So there is a gap between the two front seat, and since we were so crowded in the back I was almost pushed forward between the two front seats.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How far was the end of the sniper rifle from your face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The butt was on the floor, and the end of the sniper rifle was no more than five centimetres from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you describe the end of the sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: It had something black screwed onto it on top. At that time, I didn't know what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after the three of you got into the car with Milan Lukic and the other three soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He drove out along the 22nd December Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After he drove along the 22nd of December Street, where did he go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We turned left towards the very centre of town, but before turning we encountered in the street the same Serb man who had been fishing that time when we were watching when Kasim Fehric was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was anything said in the car when you were passing this Serb man, and what was said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. Milan Lukic said to his mate in the front seat something like, "I almost killed that man cause I didn't know he was a Serb."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after you passed that Serb man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We continued along the 22nd December Street, and we turned left by the supermarket towards the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What occurred after you reached the centre of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan Lukic did not drive through the centre himself. Instead, he went around another settlement towards the old bridge in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe what happened as you approached the old bridge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: In the meantime, as we were approaching Milan asked us if we could swim, and that's when we got near the old bridge, and there were a lot of people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At some point in time did the red Passat stop on the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, briefly, in the very middle of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was said in the car when it stopped on the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: That man who sat next to Milan said to Milan that it was better to drive to the new bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did the car then go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We crossed the old bridge, turned right, and drove along the Drina to the new bridge, and in the meantime we had to answer questions by Milan as to whether we were able to swim.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened when you reached the new bridge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We stopped almost in the middle of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After the red Passat stopped, what occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I'll quote Milan Lukic. "We're out of petrol. We have to take the Drina River. It's true it's a bit cold, but never mind."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic say anything after that to anyone else in the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He turned to the two young Serb soldiers who were sitting in the back with us, and he told them, I'll quote again: "The faint-hearted should stay in the car."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After Milan Lukic made those comments, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The three of us got out of the car and so did Milan Lukic and the passenger in the front, whereas the young Serb soldiers remained sitting in the back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did anyone approach Milan Lukic and this other soldier and the three of you after you got out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: A man who was on the left bank by the bridge in some sort of guards' booth. A Serb soldier came out of that booth and told Milan, "What on earth are you doing? Don't you see these are children?"

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did Milan do after that was said to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan and the man who sat next to him started yelling and started pointed their guns at that man, and he had to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After this man withdrew, what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan threatened him that he would kill him, too, and he told him to go on doing his job.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did this man eventually leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after the man left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan told us to stand by the railing of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How far were you from Milan Lukic at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: More than two metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who was standing on your left and right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Samir was to my right, Ajvaz was to my left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan asked us if we had any money or gold jewellery on us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after he asked for gold or money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: When he saw we had nothing, he told me since I was the tallest amongst the three of us, he told me to go over the railing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you do when Milan Lukic said this to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I had lost all my faculties. I couldn't do anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did Milan Lukic do next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He told me very loudly to go over the side of the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did you respond?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I stood frozen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He walked by me and grabbed Samir, who had a tracksuit on. He grabbed the top of his tracksuit. His rifle was on his shoulder, so he grabbed Samir and threw him over the side of the bridge. Samir tried to grab the side of the bridge, but it had been raining in Visegrad before the 14th. The railing was made of iron. It was slippery, so he slipped and fell into the water.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you see Samir hit the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you see if he was able to come to the surface?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, because I was leaning against the railing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How far were you from Milan Lukic at this time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: One metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was Milan Lukic to your left or right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He was right in front of me, right in front of me and this boy Ajvaz from Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did Milan Lukic do after Samir was thrown into the water?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He took the sniper rifle off his shoulder. He -- he took his rifle into his hands, stabilising it against the railing, and he hit Samir with one bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you see him fire the sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, because he was right next to me, not even half a metre away from me when he approach the railing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you see come from the end of the gun when it was fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I felt something like the smell of gunpowder, but it was not very loud when he fired the shot. Even we who were standing right next to him couldn't hear the normal sound of a -- of a gunfire shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How many times did he shoot at Samir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you then look towards the Drina where Samir was at?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. We looked into the water, all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I saw Samir for two or three seconds, and then he drowned. Only in the spot where he had been a second ago I saw a circle of blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was Samir killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after Samir was killed by Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Then this little boy from Foca started crying and begging Milan to spare him. He started taking out some small coins from his pocket, and I remember there was one banknote of small denomination fell into a puddle as it fell from his hands. Milan, of course, didn't want to take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: At that moment, Milan told him not to worry, that he won't do anything to him. And the same second he said that, he did the same thing as he had done earlier to Samir. This little boy was even lighter than Samir, and he was just thrown over the railing into the river. But before throwing him, as this little boy was proffering the money he had, he was also saying he couldn't swim.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after this little boy was thrown over the railing by Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan turned to face the car. All the four doors of the car were open, wide open, and he said something to the man who had gotten out with him, that Serb. He said something like, "The little boy can't swim and he'll drown." And then the Serb in the front seat looked at the Drina River. I was leaning on the railing, and as that man looked I also looked, and I saw this little boy from Foca surfacing and struggling with the current. The water was very high and rather wild. The boy was struggling to stay on the surface, and then the man who had gotten out of the car with Milan cocked his automatic rifle and cursed, saying that the little boy from Foca was lying when he said he couldn't swim, and he fired something like 10 to 15 rounds at the boy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When this other man fired his gun, how loud was it in comparison to the rifle that Milan Lukic fired?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Much louder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can he say whether any of the shot fired at the little boy hit him?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-89, as Judge Robinson just asked you, do you know whether or not any of these shots that were fired by this other man who was with Milan Lukic hit the boy from Foca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, because both of us were looking into the water, and the little boy from Foca disappeared. I don't know exactly how many bullets hit him, but I know he was hit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, how much longer will you be? We're past the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if you'd like, this is -- I can break at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And then there's one topic area that I have to go through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-89, we left off discussing the shooting of the boy from Foca. At some point in time, did Milan Lukic and this other man return you to the Volkswagen Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened when you got back into the Volkswagen Passat?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. Before that, I'd like to find out how was the decision, if any, made for him to -- to go to the Passat instead of being thrown over the river. Was there any conversation relating to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: VG-89, could you please describe the events after the other soldier shot at the boy from Foca to when you got to the Volkswagen Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: As I said earlier, all the four doors of that Volkswagen Passat were wide open all that time. Later, after the little boy from Foca was killed, Milan Lukic grabbed my shirt behind my neck, and at that moment I thought he was going to throw me into the river as he had done with the two boys before me. He literally shoved me into the back seat of the Passat. To this day, I don't know why. There was no conversation between me and him. There was no conversation at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened once you were back in the Volkswagen Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Everyone got back into the car where they had sat earlier. Milan took the driver's seat. The other man sat in front next to him. I was again in the back seat. Milan started the car, and we started driving across the bridge, and at that moment he turned on the music in the car really loud.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where did Milan Lukic take you then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We turned towards the Mezalin. He took me to the MUP building in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you arrive at the MUP building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Before 5.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to talk to you about your stay at the MUP building in Visegrad. For approximately how many days after you arrived on the 14th of June, 1992, were you at the MUP building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When Milan Lukic and the other Serb soldiers brought you to the MUP building, could you please describe what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Milan took me upstairs to some sort of reception desk in the MUP building, which is right to the left as you climb the stairs, and there was a policeman sitting there, a policeman nicknamed Razonoda. This Razonoda asked me who I was. He took a piece of paper to write my name down, and he was about to ask me who was with me, and then Milan Lukic said it didn't matter, like, it doesn't matter who had been with me. Those persons were not important. And after that, Milan Lukic ordered that policeman to keep me there in gaol and that no one, really no one, was allowed to let me out without his permission. And after that, Milan Lukic left, and that policeman led me to an empty room on the same floor where the reception was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you see Milan Lukic at all later at the police station after he left you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Not that day. Not on the 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately what time was it that Milan Lukic left the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: We stayed for about five minutes in the police station so that Milan Lukic left the station around 5.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Over the course of the next three days, did you see Milan Lukic again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Every day for the next few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You said that you did not see Milan Lukic again on the 14th of June, 1992. What was the next day that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The 15th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where were you kept the evening of the 14th of June through to the 15th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: In that empty room to which you get as you go down the hall from the reception desk on the right. There were bars on the door. It was not a regular door.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were there any windows to this room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes, one small window overlooking the street, the bridge, and the Borac department store.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you able to tell whether it was day or night based on the fact that there was a window to your cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you saw Milan Lukic on the 15th of June, 1992, was it day or night-time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: It was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened when you saw Milan Lukic on the 15th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Between that night on the 14th and the morning of the 15th, more Muslims were brought to that room, and Milan demanded that they stand up and sing Chetnik songs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did Milan Lukic enter the cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: No. He was standing in the door.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where were you inside of the cell when Milan Lukic asked you to sing these songs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: I was in the corner behind those bars, in a small corner where he could not see me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after Milan Lukic requested that the songs were to be sung?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He recognised one of the men there. The man was about 55. Milan addressed him by name saying, "Nijaz, where is your son?" That son was a schoolmate of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did this man respond?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He said his son had left for Austria, to live there. And then Milan told him he wouldn't kill him - I mean the elderly man - and that man started thanking him or something, and then Milan said, "I won't kill you. I'll slit your throat."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened after that conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Someone called out Milan's name, and he dashed outside from where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you see Milan Lukic again on the 15th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did you next see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was he with anyone when you saw him the next time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: With the same man who had taken us to the bridge, who sat in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was this the man who shot at the boy from Foca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You've described him earlier, but could you just please make clear his physical description.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This man who shot at the boy from Foca who was with Milan Lukic on the 15th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Rather short, not over 170 centimetres tall, wearing camouflage, an automatic rifle, black hair and black moustache; age, about 35.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened when Milan Lukic and this other man came to your cell in the late afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Again, he appeared at the door. There's one thing that I forgot to say earlier on. All those who were locked up inside had to give away any money that they had on them, their watches or whatever, and place it all in the middle of the room. Milan didn't notice me, so he spoke to the two young men that they'd taken off the bus. That's what they told me in prison because they had been on their way from Serbia to Konjic. They were heading home because they had a job in Serbia. He said, "Is there a young man anywhere around in this prison?" And they said, "Yes, there is one." I was there in the corner, and he told me to stay. I walked up to the door. He was standing just outside the cell and I was still inside. He offered me his hand. He shook hands with me and said that he -- he wanted to tell me something about the money on that heap in the middle of the room. He said, Do you know Risto Perisic, a teacher from Visegrad? And I said, Yes, I know him, and he said, When you see him pass by, give him all this money and tell him it's from Milan Lukic. He also said that he wouldn't allow anyone to lay a finger on me in this prison. He told everyone not to as much as touch me, and then he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did this interaction between you and Milan Lukic occur, on the 14th of June or on the 15th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: 15th of June. That was the second time he came.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you say the second time he came, was this the time that you interacted with him in the morning or afternoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Late afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you ever observe Milan Lukic interact with Risto Perisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The 16th of June. They were passing through that hallway to some offices or whatever they had there on that floor. I saw the two of them talk and receding down that hallway. However, as for the money that he had told me to give to Risto, well, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This hallway that you observed them in, was this the hallway that was in front of your cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you tell the tone of voice that they were speaking to each other in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: It was a friendly tone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was this different than the tone that Milan Lukic had with all the other individuals that you observed over the three days at the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: It was quite different from the conversation that Milan had had with the policeman Razonoda. He had literally ordered that policeman what to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to take you back to the 15th of June, 1992. Did anything else occur when you saw Milan Lukic in the late afternoon than what you've already described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: There was mistreatment at the prison, but I didn't see Milan Lukic there. I don't think he was there when they were actually beating those men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who beat those men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Local Serbs who happened to be on at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you tell if these local Serbs were policemen or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Some were policemen, and some had just joined the paramilitary units as soon as the war began.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were any of these people the people that you observed with Milan Lukic on any prior dates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When did these beatings occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: On the 14th, the evening of the 14th. That's when it began, and it went on until I left prison early in the morning on the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to take you to the 16th of June, 1992. You mentioned that you saw Milan Lukic again on that day. What time of day did you see him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: That afternoon. There was an interview first. They had me for an interview, and they wanted some Muslim names from me who were apparently hiding, and they placed a knife in my throat threatening to slit my throat unless I told them. But Milan Lukic wasn't in the room. It was after I'd returned that Milan Lukic was back.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who were these individuals that held a knife up to your throat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Soldiers of the JNA wearing JNA uniforms, and those were different from the uniforms that Milan Lukic and his men were wearing. These were younger ones; they aged 18 or 19. He placed the military knife under my throat, and he said that we Muslims used to be Serbs, but the Turks converted us 500 years before. He said they'd have all the Muslims killed, and those they didn't kill would be reconverted to orthodoxy. He asked me a question, but then I said nothing. But I spent about 15 or 20 minutes there, and then they sent me back to my cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How long after you returned to your cell did Milan Lukic appear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Some one and a half hours later, perhaps two hours later. I wasn't wearing a watch, and I couldn't really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was anyone else in your cell when Milan Lukic arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. A total of eight persons. Seven men, one lady.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were all the other people in your cell Muslims also?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What happened when Milan Lukic came to your cell on the 16th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Again, he wanted everyone to sing Chetnik songs. Again, he called me to walk up to the door, and he offered his hand for me to shake, and I saw him wear a large golden ring. I could actually feel the ring as I was shaking his hand. He didn't mistreat me or anything. He mistreated the other people there but not me, not at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How did Milan Lukic mistreat the other people that were with you on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He was telling them that he would have them all killed, their throats slit. He was screaming at this policeman to get him the key so he could get into the room and kill everyone and slit everyone's throats, kill all those people there. Some had been subjected to beatings already. The night between the 14th and the 15th, there had been a lot of beating going on in that prison, but I wasn't allowed to watch what was going on. For those two nights, they were beating those Muslim men, and while they were doing that they took me to another room so that I couldn't see for myself. I couldn't see it with my own eyes. I was just given some pieces of cloth to mop up the floors and the walls when I returned to the cell. There was blood all over the place and body parts all over the floor and the walls. There was no room there to even sit down because there was blood and body parts all over the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you -- did they make you clean up the cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Milan Lukic was wearing a large gold ring on the 16th of June. Was this the first occasion that you observed him with this gold ring?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After the 16th of June, did you see Milan Lukic at all at the police station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: The evening of the 16th, late that evening Milan Lukic returned along with this man who was always with him, the man who had killed the young man from Foca at the bridge. Milan didn't go into the cell; rather, the other Serb did. There was a low table made of wood and a small bench next to that table. He told me to sit down on that bench, this Serb. Once I did, he starred telling me that the Muslims were killing Serbs in Gorazde and that the Muslims were killing Serb children. And he said something about the dam in Visegrad, some kilometres from the town, how they kept finding bodies of dead Serb children there, whose throats had been slit, from Gorazde. And he said there would be a quid pro quo thing and that for every Serb child that was killed they would kill a Muslim, and this, he said, was why they were killing all the Muslims, including the children. I didn't answer back. He realised that, so he didn't stay for too long. He was there for maybe 15 or 20 minutes, and then he left. This was late at night, the 16th of June. At daybreak on the 17th, I was released from Visegrad prison, unbeknownst to Milan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who released you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Mirko Lakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who is Mirko Lakic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: He was my next-door neighbour. Before the war, he worked as a butcher in Visegrad. This was a well-regarded Serb family from Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you proceed to leave with your mother on the 17th of June, 1992, from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Yes. I was scared to death. I knew that if I stayed, that would be the end of me as soon as they got their hands on me again, so we had no choice but to leave. While leaving Visegrad on that bus, again, Milan got onto the bus. This was one of the most critical moments for me, one of the most dangerous moments. I was sitting at the rear of the bus, in the corner, and Milan Lukic was looking for some people named Sabanovic. I remember that clearly. There was a rather young girl three rows away from me. She couldn't have been over 20 years of age at the time. She had a kerchief that she was wearing on her head, and there were some elderly people seated along the aisle in the middle of the bus, some people who were unable to move or use the seats. The bus was chock-a-block with people. Milan didn't go all the way to the bottom of the bus. He remained at the door. And then he told the girl to remove the kerchief because he thought that she was a young man in disguise or something. I thought he would walk all the way down the aisle, so I slid off the seat in order to hide behind the seat right in front of me, and I hid behind a bag, but then fortunately Milan Lukic got off the bus and was gone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During your three days at the Visegrad police station, did you ever observe anyone give Milan Lukic an order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: After you left Visegrad on the 17th of June, 1992, have you ever lived in that municipality again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-89
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What about the converse of that? Did he ever observe Milan Lukic give an order to anybody at the police station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. And what are the circumstances in which that order was given? To whom was it given and when, and what was the order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
